title: AgriManager: A Framework and Benchmark for LLM-RL Generalization in Agricultural Management
abstract: arXiv:2611.28844v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Agricultural management is heterogeneous along two axes. The first is distributional shift within a fixed task interface: weather, crops, and prices vary across years and locations while sensors, actions, and objective stay fixed. The second is structural shift across interfaces: different farms expose different observed variables, available actions, and management objectives. We formalize the second axis as schema shift: variation in the policy-facing schema $\Sigma = (\Sigma_O, \Sigma_A, \Sigma_R)$ between training and deployment. We test whether LLM-RL generalizes across both axes with AgriManager, to our knowledge the first framework that trains LLM policies with RL across multiple process-based crop simulators, unifying DSSAT, WOFOST, and Cycles. We design a three-tier generalization ladder: Tier 1 within-schema distributional shift, Tier 2 single-axis schema shift along $\Sigma_O / \Sigma_A / \Sigma_R$, Tier 3 compositional schema

translated_title: AgriManager：一个面向LLM-RL在农业管理中泛化能力的框架与基准测试
translated_abstract: 农业管理在两个维度上呈现异质性。第一个是固定任务接口内的分布偏移：天气、作物和价格会随年份和地点而变化，而传感器、动作和目标保持不变。第二个是不同接口之间的结构性偏移：不同农场暴露出不同的观测变量、可用动作和管理目标。我们将第二个维度形式化为“模式偏移”：即策略所面对的模式 $\Sigma = (\Sigma_O, \Sigma_A, \Sigma_R)$ 在训练与部署之间的变化。我们利用 AgriManager 检验 LLM-RL 是否能在这两个维度上实现泛化。据我们所知，AgriManager 是首个跨越多个基于过程的作物模拟器（统一了 DSSAT、WOFOST 和 Cycles）用强化学习训练 LLM 策略的框架。我们设计了三层泛化阶梯：第1层为模式内分布偏移，第2层为沿 $\Sigma_O / \Sigma_A / \Sigma_R$ 的单轴模式偏移，第3层为组合式模式偏移（原文摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 该论文提出了 AgriManager，这是首个跨多个基于过程的作物模拟器（DSSAT、WOFOST、Cycles）用强化学习训练LLM农业管理策略的框架与基准，并设计了涵盖分布偏移与模式偏移的三层泛化阶梯来系统评估LLM-RL的泛化能力。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces AgriManager, the first framework and benchmark that trains LLM policies with RL across multiple process-based crop simulators (DSSAT, WOFOST, and Cycles), and designs a three-tier generalization ladder spanning distributional shift and schema shift to systematically evaluate LLM-RL generalization in agricultural management.
